module_title: Cell Organelles and Their Famous Nicknames
introduction: Inside the cell, there are specialized, tiny structures called 'Cell Organelles'. Just like organs in our body perform specific tasks, organelles keep the cell alive. Examiners love asking for their famous 'nicknames'.

core_concepts.title: Mitochondria
core_concepts.description:
Nickname: 'Powerhouse of the Cell'. 
Function: It is the site of cellular respiration. It generates and stores energy in the form of 'ATP' (Adenosine Triphosphate). 
Special Feature: Mitochondria are semi-autonomous; they have their own DNA and Ribosomes.

core_concepts.title: Ribosomes
core_concepts.description:
Nickname: 'Protein Factory of the Cell'. 
Function: They link amino acids together to synthesize (create) proteins. 
Special Feature: They are the smallest cell organelles and do NOT have any membrane around them.

core_concepts.title: Lysosomes
core_concepts.description:
Nickname: 'Suicide Bags' or 'Digestive Bags'. 
Function: They contain powerful hydrolytic enzymes capable of digesting cellular waste, foreign bacteria, and worn-out organelles. If the cell gets damaged, the lysosome bursts and its enzymes digest its own cell (hence, suicide bags).

core_concepts.title: Plastids (Found ONLY in Plants)
core_concepts.description:
1. Chloroplast: Contains green chlorophyll; performs photosynthesis. Nickname: 'Kitchen of the Cell'. 
2. Chromoplast: Provides attractive colors (red, yellow, orange) to flowers and fruits (e.g., Lycopene gives red color to tomatoes). 
3. Leucoplast: Colorless plastid used for 'storing' food (starch, oils, proteins), mostly found in roots.

core_concepts.title: Golgi Apparatus (Golgi Body)
core_concepts.description:
Nickname: 'Traffic Police' or 'Post Office of the Cell'. 
Function: It packages, modifies, and dispatches materials (proteins and lipids) synthesized by the ER to their correct destinations inside or outside the cell.

important_entities.name: Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)
important_entities.description:
1. Rough ER (RER): Has ribosomes attached to its surface (making it look rough). It is responsible for 'Protein Synthesis'. 
2. Smooth ER (SER): Lacks ribosomes. It is responsible for 'Lipid (Fat) Synthesis' and helps in detoxifying poisons and drugs in the liver.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: The 'Cell Membrane' (Plasma Membrane) is found in BOTH plant and animal cells (made of lipids and proteins). However, the rigid 'Cell Wall' is found ONLY in plants, fungi, and bacteria. Animal cells do NOT have a cell wall.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Mito = Power, Ribo = Protein, Lyso = Suicide.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Mitochondria = Powerhouse. Ribosome = Protein factory. Lysosome = Suicide bag.

exam_strategy_tips: A legendary Railway (RRB) question: 'What is known as the energy currency of the cell?' Answer: ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate).
